digest.component_or_area: MCP error surface + library error classification
propositions: MCP tool failures currently surface as unstructured prose in exception messages or ad-hoc partial shapes, while the CLI emits a structured error_envelope discriminator; agents cannot reliably distinguish error types across interfaces without pattern-matching English text

The error code vocabulary is scattered across CLI call sites (reads_cli.py, claim.py, transition.py, etc.) with no central registry or library-side classifier, violating the requirement that a code cannot exist on one interface only

The library interface exposes no machine error discriminator; RebarError/ConcurrencyError/TrackerRootError do not carry a uniform error code, so a cross-interface test comparing library + CLI + MCP has no library-side value to compare

MCP must emit the same vocabulary codes as the CLI (ticket_not_found, concurrency_conflict, claim_failed, etc.) sourced from a single shared error_code_for classifier, verified by tests that drive the same failure through all three interfaces and assert identical machine codes
The error_envelope schema marks input required but MCP failures without a resolved target have no input; input must be optional in the schema while CLI continues passing it unconditionally

Two MCP tools return ad-hoc soft-error shapes (explain_criterion returns {error, kind}; LLM returns {error, resolution_class, retryable, diagnostic}) that must be migrated to carry vocabulary error codes while preserving the agent-branching fields (kind, resolution_class, retryable, diagnostic) as additional fields
